name: CA-50
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Scott Peters seeking re-election with large cash advantage
Republican Steve Cohen has minimal fundraising and no outside support
Markets price a Democratic win at about 96%
model.rationale: The district leans Democratic by 10 points, incumbent Peters holds a large financial edge with no outside opposition, and prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96%. With no polls or expert ratings available, the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 21 points stands.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much narrower race or unexpected outside spending against Peters would warrant a shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Scott Peters, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking re-election in a San Diego-area district that leans Democratic by about 10 points. He advanced to the general election and has raised over $1.8 million with $2.6 million on hand, while Republican Steve Cohen reports no fundraising figures and draws no outside support. Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability near 96 percent.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap. Those all point the same direction, making Peters a strong favorite, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty about the exact margin.
